Dashboard Visual Review

7 Oct 2026, desktop at 1440px. The first item is built on branch feat/dbim-and-proposed-default and is not merged. Every other "After" is a mock-up made by changing the live page in the browser. No code has changed for those yet, and nothing changes until you approve. Approved items go to the Figma handoff first, then to the build.

Built on the branchMinistry › Our Performance › Beneficiary Dashboard

The proposed dashboard opens by default

Before, the address opened the current Beneficiary Dashboard and the proposed one needed ?version=proposed. After, the bare address opens the proposed one. The demo rail's Version switch (Proposed first, then Current) opens the old page at ?version=current. Old ?version=proposed links still work. The old per-portal pages' breadcrumb returns to the old page. DBIM was already the default website design, so nothing changed there.

Proposed · your instructionDemo rail › View As

Two roles only: Public and Officer

The sheet has two audiences, Pre-Login (Public) and Post-Login (Officer). The six-role list in the demo rail goes. Being signed in decides the role, and the officer's account decides the scope: which programmes, and which State or District.

Proposed · your instructionDashboard › Officer Login

Officer Login asks only for User ID and password

The Office dropdown let the person choose their own scope, which a real login never does. In the prototype, the six offices become demo accounts (one User ID each) kept in the project's fixture file. An unknown User ID is refused, and the password is not checked, since this is a prototype. The description now says the account decides what is shown.

ProposedEvery programme page

Back link first, less empty space above the banner

'All Programmes' sat under the page heading and then left about 70px of blank space before the banner. Moved above the heading, it reads as the way back, and the banner moves up.

ProposedSMILE › Outcomes (Trends gets the same)

A single figure beside a chart becomes that chart's headline

A lone figure card was stretched to the chart's height, leaving a tall empty box (Persons Rehabilitated, and Year-on-Year Growth under Trends). The figure now heads the chart it summarises, and the chart takes the full row. The bars are also sorted largest first, which is a reorder inside the card. In the build the chart is redrawn at the wider size. The mock-up only shows the bar list because the line chart cannot be resized in a mock-up.

ProposedWhere the Scheme Works, NMBA Coverage and others

Figures in a row of cards sit on one line

A two-line card title pushed its figure 20px lower than its neighbours' (17, 38 against 112, 312). The title area now always holds two lines, so every figure lines up.

ProposedSenior Citizens Welfare

Sections side by side start their cards at the same height

'Other Initiatives' has a one-line heading beside two-line ones, so its card started 30px higher. Headings in a shared row now take the same height.

ProposedSHRESHTA

SHRESHTA's banner shows its two figures

The right half of the banner was empty because SHRESHTA has no single-figure tiles. It now shows its two public indicators (No. of Beneficiaries Benefited, Total Funds Released), labelled as in the sheet, as every other programme's banner does.

ProposedDashboard overview

One 'Year by Year Trends' section, not two near-identical ones

'Year by Year Trends' was followed by 'Year on Year Report': two headings saying the same thing, one after the other. The three year-wise charts become the second row of the first section.

ProposedDashboard overview

Share of Fund Release as ranked bars

In the donut, one slice is 69% and six are under 2%, so most slices cannot be seen. Ranked bars show every scheme with its amount and share. Same figures, same order.

ProposedDashboard overview › State/UT-wise Figures

Lowest five States/UTs without empty bar tracks

On the national scale, the lowest five draw bars 1px long, which read as broken. They keep the value and rank ('32 of 36') and lose the empty track.

ProposedSMILE › Skill & Training

Status breakdowns use status colours

'Completed' was drawn in red, which on this estate means rejected or failing. Completed becomes green, In Progress stays blue and Discontinued turns grey. Red is also the chart palette's second colour (R.E. in DAPSC, Female in the gender ring). Changing the palette is a SAMAVESH decision, to be made in the Figma library first, so it is flagged here and not changed.

ProposedDAPSC › Funds

DAPSC Funds: no empty R.E. stub, signed differences

2026-27 has no R.E. yet, and the chart drew a dashed empty box with a dash for it. That bar is now left out. The Mandated Allocation table shows the difference as ▲ +0.8 / ▼ −0.7 in green or red, with tighter rows, so the ten Ministries fit without the table running on.

Looked at, not proposed

Home page social media cards

The grey bars in the four social media cards look like content still loading. They are a deliberate stand-in, though: third-party posts load only when the reader presses "Show Latest Posts". A better resting state needs a DBIM design decision, so no mock-up is offered.
